attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No Yang-Mills proof yet gives the uniform reflected Wilson hairpin boundary OPE producing H,K and remainders for the locked gauge-invariant algebra.
steps: For fixed collar, regulated positivity plus RG convergence puts each finite reflected Wilson matrix N_delta in the closed PSD cone.
If additive contacts vanish, collar collapse factors as N_delta=B_delta circ M_delta; hence the intended same-theory matrix is M_delta=B_delta^{[-1]} circ N_delta.
After diagonal normalization q_delta tends to J. Splitting C^n=Ce plus e^perp, the Schur complement of the vacuum eigenvalue n gives epsilon PHP plus the second-order correction.
Thus negative PHP on e^perp, or negative corrected A2 on ker(PHP), is a valid finite obstruction; positive reduced coefficients with gaps promote the block.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-matrix argument is valid conditional linear algebra; the missing analytic input is control of non-Abelian Wilson collars at the reflection plane without hidden boundary renormalization.

assumptions: Regulated reflection positivity and RG convergence give N_delta>=0 for each fixed collar and convergence of all finite reflected entries.
B_delta has no zero entries and positive diagonal; diagonal trace continuity has removed positive additive contacts.
After diagonal normalization, q_delta=J+epsilon H+epsilon^2 K+O(epsilon^3) in operator norm, with H,K Hermitian and e=n^{-1/2}1.
The O(epsilon^3) remainder is uniform for the locked finite Wilson block.
definitions: source object: finite reflected Wilson collar OS matrices N_delta from regulated reflection-positive lattice/RG Schwinger forms, with boundary anomaly matrices B_delta and collar scale delta>0.
target object: continuum OS quadratic form on the same finite Wilson observables at the reflection plane.
controlled interface: q_delta=hat N_delta oslash hat B_delta finite matrix PSD tests after diagonal normalization and removal of proven additive contacts.
same-theory condition: B_delta records only collar renormalization of locked observables; no boundary operator, quotient gauge algebra, or Wilson renormalization convention is changed.

equations.label: exact quotient criterion
equations.valid_when: valid when collar collapse is purely multiplicative and B has no zero entries; this is the exact finite same-theory OS test.

equations.label: vacuum expansion
equations.valid_when: valid after diagonal/one-body normalization and a uniform Wilson boundary OPE in collar scale epsilon.

equations.label: second Feshbach gate
equations.valid_when: valid if A1 is PSD and has a spectral gap off its kernel; a negative A1 or A2 gives a finite Wilson falsifier.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find locked hairpin observables with q_delta expansion whose first nonzero reduced Feshbach coefficient has a negative vector; then collar positivity does not imply target OS positivity.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Replaces vague boundary anomaly talk by finite PSD quotient and Feshbach gates; it can certify valid OS transfer or exhibit a normalization-safe mixed Wilson falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite locked Wilson collar block, same-theory OS positivity after collar collapse is finite PSD of the Schur quotient. Near the vacuum rank-one matrix, the first negative vacuum-Feshbach reduced coefficient is a normalization-safe falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the RG topology cannot control finite reflected Wilson OPE remainders or if boundary counterterms are unavoidable.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote when H,K and the first nonzero Feshbach reductions are proved PSD for a dense locked Wilson core.
control_decision.reason: The branch has a precise finite-matrix bridge and a concrete analytic gap: Wilson hairpin boundary OPE with uniform remainders.

dependency_updates.description: Fixed-collar closed-cone passage remains formal; the boundary step is now finite Schur-quotient positivity plus Feshbach reductions.
The Wilson core must be locked before quotienting; one-body diagonal congruences are harmless but boundary operators are not.
It must control reflected Wilson boundary OPE remainders in operator norm for each finite block, not only distributional entries.
Compute H,K and higher reduced coefficients for reflected hairpin collars with uniform error bounds.

falsifiers: falsifier: a computed hairpin block has v^*Hv<0 for some v perpendicular to 1.
falsifier: PHP>=0 but v^*A2v<0 on ker(PHP), with the -n^{-1}Hee^*H correction included.
falsifier: q_delta has a negative 3 by 3 determinant although every pairwise damping inequality holds.
falsifier: collar collapse requires a boundary counterterm or altered Wilson renormalization not encoded in B_delta.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 229 makes the obstruction an exact finite quotient problem near the vacuum matrix. The valid test is not B alone, nor pairwise damping, nor raw PKP. Remove the rank-one OS direction, then use Feshbach reductions; the first negative reduced coefficient is the genuine same-theory falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the epsilon and epsilon^2 boundary OPE coefficients for three mirror Wilson hairpins with common footprint, normalize q_delta, and test PHP plus the corrected A2.

The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
